observations: A mouth with two rows of white teeth separated by a dark gap sits in the lower center, outlined in red and black against a black ground; the upper and lower tooth rows are drawn with vertical white strokes divided by thin black lines.
Two round eyes with red rims, black irises, and yellow-green pupils are placed side by side in the upper center, set against a dark field scattered with bright green dots.

A vertical column of yellow-outlined ovals, each containing a blue shape, runs down the left border; a matching column of yellow rectangles with orange-red centers lines the right border and bottom edge.
reading: The face is stripped to its loudest parts: eyes that bulge with yellow-green rings and a bared mouth whose two tooth rows read as a grin or a grimace. The border columns of repeating ovals and rectangles hold the scene in a frame that feels more like a marquee than a margin. The dark interior, scattered with green dots and loose pink scribbles, reads as noise behind the face rather than space around it.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between #66 and #68 in both title and recorded creation order. Where #66 fills its field with a warm-toned animal form, #67 pulls back to a flat, bordered composition built on repeating units.

connections.reason: nnxyz nnotb #68 shares the face-centered layout and a row of repeating rectangular units along an edge, but replaces the flat black ground and bold color with layered scribble lines and muted olive tones, making the contrast in surface density visible.

lookingQuestion: The border columns of ovals and rectangles use the same yellow outline but different interior colors on each side—what does that difference do to the way your eye moves around the edge?
ambiguities: Title-derived order and recorded creation order align here, but the metadata notes gaps and variants exist elsewhere in the nnotb family, so adjacency cannot confirm a making sequence.
The nifty-faces comparison shares a dense multi-element composition but no specific formal unit matches the border columns or face structure of #67 closely enough to support a useful connection.
